data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Ireland performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably comparing 2022 to 2018 and trends since 2012). PISA uses rotated two-hour subject tests with different students receiving different item sets, plus a background questionnaire for students and a principal questionnaire for school context. For Ireland, 5,569 students in 170 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, representing about 65,500 15-year-olds (estimated as ~100% of the population of 15-year-olds). The factsheet reports mean performance differences versus the OECD average, proficiency-level attainment (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6 shares), and subgroup patterns such as socioeconomic gradients and gender differences. It also flags a technical concern: Ireland’s student response rate fell below PISA’s minimum target, and non-response bias analyses suggest reported mean scores may be slightly higher than hypothetical means including non-respondents.
